pr_title: Removing kubectl get output e2e test
pr_body:
**What type of PR is this?**
/kind failing-test

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
This was primarily to prevent new API resources being added without proper kubectl integration. This test has been replaced in 1.18 and is now irrelevant (and flaky) here.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #88335

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:
```release-note
NONE
```

/sig cli
/priority critical-urgent
/assign @liggitt @tpepper @alejandrox1
pr_comments: Since the point of the test is to catch new resources, and https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88966 will do that in 1.19, and no new in-tree resources are introduced in patch versions, I would probably just delete this test from this branch.
@liggitt Good call, I've updated this PR to do that.

[APPROVALNOTIFIER] This PR is **APPROVED** This pull-request has been approved by: *liggitt*, *robscott* The full list of commands accepted by this bot can be found [here](https://go.k8s.io/bot-commands?repo=kubernetes%2Fkubernetes). The pull request process is described [here](https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/owners.md#the-code-review-process)
Needs approval from an approver in each of these files: - ~~[test/e2e/kubectl/OWNERS](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/release-1.17/test/e2e/kubectl/OWNERS)~~ [liggitt] Approvers can indicate their approval by writing `/approve` in a comment Approvers can cancel approval by writing `/approve cancel` in a comment

In order to bring test grid green ahead of tomorrow's planned patch release we're going to merge this, even though it's a tad close to release.  Risk is minor given nature of PR (test only on a fast running and frequent test) and ability to revert if for some reason the system goes amazingly emergent and merging this truly breaks something else.
Slack discussion here for add'l context: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C2C40FMNF/p1583975966431100

A rundown of this job for posterity
```
- args:
  - --check-version-skew=false
  - --extract=ci/k8s-stable1
  - --extract=ci/latest
  - --skew
  - --test_args=--ginkgo.focus=Kubectl --ginkgo.skip=\[Serial\] --minStartupPods=8

xref: https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/tree/master/kubetest#upgrade-skew-kubemark

So this test goes from ci/latest (1.18) to ci/k8s-stable1 (1.17.x).
Also, this job sets `--test_args` but NO `--test`.

> You will be able to find 2 new directories named `kubernetes` and `kubernetes_skew` at current directory. `kubernetes` is the directory corresponding to release indicated by first --extract flag, while `kubernetes_skew` corresponds to second flag.

* `kubernetes_skew/` contains 1.18

> "skew", false, "If true, run tests in another version at ../kubernetes/kubernetes_skew"

This job sets `--skew` so it will run tests in 1.18.
Which i think means there is something missing because running the tests from 1.18 should work (?).

Inside of the job, it starts by running latest from master and then it runs the follwoing
```
kubetest --test --test_args=--ginkgo.focus=Kubectl --ginkgo.skip=\[Serial\] 
  --minStartupPods=8 --report-dir=/workspace/_artifacts --disable-log-dump=true

Right after that skew is completed then the tests are run
```
I0306 02:22:55.936] Mar  6 02:22:55.831: INFO: e2e test version: v1.17.4-beta.0.34+23eb2180c65472
I0306 02:22:55.937] Mar  6 02:22:55.876: INFO: kube-apiserver version: v1.19.0-alpha.0.599+edf460bc0f5082
```

https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/d766f5c0c27cea83aefcbbeed9b79ab8b0da0225/kubetest/extract_k8s.go#L145

https://github.com/kubernetes/test-infra/blob/master/kubetest/e2e.go#L186

The `--extract=ci/k8s-stable1` downloads and extracts this into the `kubernetes` dir
The second `--extract=ci/latest` renames the `k8s-stable1` `kubernetes` dir as `kubernetes_skew` and then downloads `latest` into a new `kubernetes`.
The `--skew` flag causes it to run tests in `kubernetes_skew`.

Thus the expected behavior is:
 * `kubernetes_skew` has `k8s-stable1`
* `kubernetes` has `latest`
* Tests run from the `kubernetes_skew` dir, aka `k8s-stable1`

Hey @alejandrox1, this test was trying to ensure that kubectl was properly configured for all Kubernetes resources. This is something that's unlikely to break after the initial setup, but is easy to miss when adding a new resource. I missed this initially when adding EndpointSlices, and this test was meant to ensure that no one else would in the future. Adding this test actually resulted in kubectl integration being fixed for ~3 other resources. With all that said, this test was poorly written, and Jordan is replacing it with a much better approach that requires a table converter to be specified for all resources (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/88966#issuecomment-597298118). 

Before that, table converters were not required (I didn't realize this was the only missing part). So someone could write all the code and unit tests for kubectl get and describe for their resources, but if they missed setting up the table converter, nothing would actually work with kubectl. Instead it would silently use the standard printer which printed out the default columns of "namespace", "name", and "created at". My test ran through all the available API resources, loaded data from the etcd test data, and then ran a `kubectl get` on the resource. The test would fail if there was an error or if the default fields were printed for a resource. I did have to add some exceptions for resources that actually only wanted the default fields or didn't have etcd test data, but that was pretty rare.

This test was definitely not designed with the idea of skew involved, and it broke here because the 1.17 tests didn't have etcd test data for a resource in the 1.18 cluster (IngressClass). This is simply because the resource didn't exist in 1.17.

So with that, sorry for the failing tests, and thanks for pinging me about this.
